I've finished the review and written 11 comments to `bench/runs/grafana_grafana-90045/vanilla/comments.json`. The file is valid JSON and nothing in the repository was changed. I found these by reading the diff; I didn't run the tests.

The most serious problem is that the new legacy writes will mostly never happen. In `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go`, the background writes to legacy start from the request's context. That context is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, which is right after the background write starts. So the legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection calls will usually fail with "context canceled". The fix is to start from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` and then add the 10-second timeout.

**Other correctness problems:**
- **Create shares the object with the background write:** `obj` goes to the legacy write after unified storage may already have changed it in place. Legacy then gets unified storage's metadata (like its resourceVersion), and the object can be modified while the response is being written from it, which is a data race. The fix is to hand over a deep copy.
- **Update sends the raw request to legacy:** it passes the original `objInfo` instead of wrapping it in `updateWrapper` with the stored result, as the old code and modes 1/2 do. Legacy computes its own version of the change and checks resourceVersions that belong to unified storage, so updates can conflict or diverge.
- **Legacy writes can arrive out of order:** each write is a separate fire-and-forget goroutine, so two quick updates, or an update then a delete, can reach legacy in the wrong order and leave it permanently inconsistent.
- **Deletes no longer reach legacy-only objects:** if the object isn't found in unified storage, the code now returns early and never deletes from legacy. Objects that exist only in legacy can't be deleted in mode 3.
- **Legacy errors are thrown away:** the background writes never log their errors, so there's no way to find which object diverged or why.

**Metrics and logging mistakes:**
- When unified storage fails in Create (line 45) and Update (line 129), the code records a legacy duration instead of a storage one.
- The legacy DeleteCollection (line 166) is recorded as a storage duration.
- Delete (line 106) labels the metric with the object name instead of the kind, which creates one metric series per deleted object.
- Delete (line 97) puts the base logger into the context instead of the one carrying name, kind and method.

**Tests:** the background goroutines can still be calling the mocks after a test has finished, so the tests are flaky and never really check the legacy calls. Also, the test case "error when creating object in the unified store fails" only passes because legacy and unified storage share one mock.
